content.content: The graph layer shall serve geometry incrementally rather than recompute the whole graph: neighbour and incident-edge lookups are answered from adjacency indexes held for the graph revision in hand, and a change to the graph recomputes only the geometry that change affects — the box of a moved node and the routes of its incident edges — never the geometry of the whole graph, and never in proportion to how many nodes are visible.
content.rationale: The prerequisite fixes only the cost relation: one and the same change costs the same however many nodes are visible. That relation is not yet a mechanism, and several mechanisms satisfy it on paper while violating it in practice, so this node commits to the mechanism that actually entails it. The mechanism is stated as three joined facts, each decidable by reading the sentence. First, lookups: neighbour and incident-edge queries are served from adjacency indexes — node to neighbours, node to incident edges — that are held for the current graph revision, so a query reads an index entry rather than scanning the edge set; the index is built when a new graph revision arrives, which is a change of the graph's data and not an interaction, and is the only work in the mechanism proportional to the graph's size. Second, change handling: applying a change recomputes exactly the geometry that change affects — a moved node's box and the routes of the edges incident to it — and nothing else; a position change therefore rebuilds no index and runs no layout or routing pass over the rest of the graph. Third, absence of remnant terms: no query, interaction event or count of visible nodes introduces work proportional to the edge set, the node set or the visible surface, so there is no full edge scan per query and no full order or layout pass per interaction; visibility affects what is drawn, not what is computed. Together these entail the prerequisite's bound rather than merely not contradicting it: the work a change costs is fixed by that change's own footprint — one node and its incident edges — and the number of visible nodes appears nowhere in the computation, so the same change costs the same at any visible count. The node does not restate the prerequisite, which says nothing about indexes or about which geometry is recomputed, and it adds no latency or frame budget, no graph-size or node-count ceiling, no library, file, protocol or rendering technique, so it decides nothing the prerequisite left open and nothing beyond this edge. The three named substitutes are excluded by the wording itself: a one-off build-time cache with no incremental update is ruled out because the indexes are held per revision and geometry is recomputed on each change, so the layer never serves a stale whole-graph snapshot as if it were current; a lazy rebuild of the whole graph is ruled out because no interaction triggers a whole-graph recomputation and a change's cost is bounded by its own footprint, not deferred to the next query; and a technique adopted for its own sake is ruled out because every element is present for a term it removes — the adjacency index removes the per-query edge scan, and the incident-edge recompute removes the full layout and routing pass — with no element serving any purpose other than the cost relation the prerequisite fixes. The commitment is therefore an elaboration of the prerequisite that closes the failure mode the edge is exposed to, and it remains silent on every decision below it.
